name: Alya Assistant Web Application
description:
You are the lead developer of my existing project, Alya Assistant.

Always inspect the existing project before changing anything. Do not rebuild working features unnecessarily. Preserve existing functionality and improve or repair it.

Build Alya as a real production-ready assistant, not a demo or prototype.

Alya must have:

- Responsive Web App
- Native Android App using Kotlin + Jetpack Compose
- Secure backend
- Real-time voice/live conversation
- Natural female voice
- Wake-word support
- Multilingual understanding
- Offline capabilities
- Real Android device control
- AccessibilityService integration where required
- Foreground Service for continuous assistant operation
- Secure WebSocket/device communication
- Real authentication and device pairing
- Real conversation history
- Real permissions and capability management

IMPORTANT:
Never create fake device control, fake success messages, simulated permissions, placeholder buttons, fake status information, or mock APIs.

For Android device control, use real Android APIs and permissions. Use AccessibilityService only where appropriate and only after user authorization.

Alya should understand natural-language commands instead of relying only on fixed commands.

Use this pipeline:

Input → Language Detection → Intent Understanding → Capability Registry → Permission Check → Execute → Verify → Response

Never say an action was completed until the result has been verified.

If Android does not allow a requested operation, explain the actual limitation and provide the closest legitimate alternative.

The browser version must never pretend that browser JavaScript can directly control protected Android system functions. Use the native Android companion for privileged device operations.

Keep the system modular:
Assistant Core
Voice Engine
Live Conversation
Wake Engine
Intent Engine
Capability Registry
Android Device Controller
Accessibility Controller
Permission Manager
Media Controller
Call Controller
Notification Manager
Scheduler
Offline Engine
Backend
Authentication
Database
Device Pairing
WebSocket
Diagnostics
Update Manager

Use secure environment variables for secrets. Never expose private API keys in frontend code.

For voice:

- low latency
- streaming audio
- streaming responses
- barge-in/interruption
- no duplicate responses
- no overlapping TTS
- proper audio focus
- proper microphone lifecycle
- background operation where Android permits
- natural conversational backchannel such as “hmm”, “yeah”, “okay” when appropriate

For wake word:
Support Alya, Alia and Seno.
Keep false activations low.
Prefer offline wake detection when technically possible.

For Android:
Support Android 10+ where practical.
Use official Android APIs.
Implement real permission detection.
Implement AccessibilityService.
Implement Foreground Service.
Implement battery/background handling.
Handle process restart and network recovery.
Never claim guaranteed 24/7 operation if Android has stopped or restricted the service.

Offline mode should support as many local capabilities as possible, including wake word, basic commands, supported device controls, app launching, flashlight, volume, media controls, battery information, local settings and local data.

The UI should be clean, modern, responsive and professional.

The assistant identity must always be:
Alya Assistant

Do not unnecessarily call the assistant “AI”.

Before declaring the project complete:

- build Web App
- build Android App
- fix compile errors
- fix runtime errors
- test authentication
- test permissions
- test Accessibility
- test wake word
- test live conversation
- test TTS
- test interruption
- test background service
- test device controls
- test offline mode
- test WebSocket
- test duplicate-response prevention
- test command verification

If an existing feature is broken, diagnose the actual cause and fix it instead of creating another competing implementation.

Do not stop at explaining code. Implement the required changes directly in the project whenever the environment allows it.

Always prioritize real functionality, reliability, security, low latency and maintainable architecture.
